verses.english: So It Was Said 49
The Book of the Twos
Chapter Two
Misconceptions
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

verses.pali: “Dvīhi, bhikkhave, diṭṭhigatehi pariyuṭṭhitā devamanussā olīyanti eke, atidhāvanti eke; cakkhumanto ca passanti.
verses.english: “Overcome by two misconceptions, mendicants, some gods and humans get stuck, some overreach, while those with vision see.
And how do some get stuck?

verses.pali: Bhavārāmā, bhikkhave, devamanussā bhavaratā bhavasammuditā tesaṁ bhavanirodhāya dhamme desiyamāne cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
verses.english: Because of love, delight, and enjoyment of existence, when the Dhamma is being taught for the cessation of existence, the minds of some gods and humans do not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.
That is how some get stuck.
And how do some overreach?

verses.pali: Bhaveneva kho paneke aṭṭīyamānā harāyamānā jigucchamānā vibhavaṁ abhinandanti—
verses.english: Some, becoming horrified, repelled, and disgusted with existence, delight in nonexistence:

verses.pali: yato kira, bho, ayaṁ attā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṁ maraṇā;
verses.english: ‘When this self is annihilated and destroyed when the body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death:

verses.pali: etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ etaṁ yāthāvanti.
verses.english: that is peaceful, that is sublime, that is how it is.’
That is how some overreach.
And how do those with vision see?
It’s when a mendicant sees what has come to be as having come to be.

verses.pali: bhūtaṁ bhūtato disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, they are practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.
That is how those with vision see.”
The Buddha spoke this matter.
On this it is said:
“Those who see what has come to be <j>as having come to be,
and see the transcendence of what has come to be,
are freed in accord with the truth,
with the ending of craving for continued existence.
They completely understand what has come to be,
rid of craving for rebirth in this or that state.
When what has come to be ceases to be,
a mendicant does not come back to future lives.”

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
